ConferenceStep.description:
One conference a cert petition was distributed for, in docket order.

Read off the petition's own "DISTRIBUTED for Conference of …" entries
(:func:`fedcourtsai.pipeline.cert_signals.conference_history`), one step per
distinct conference date, so a docket's steps are exactly the conferences
its corpus ``distribution_count`` counts. ``transition`` says how the
petition reached this conference from the one before it.

conference.description: The conference date the distribution entry names
conference.title: Conference

distributed.description: The filing date of the docket entry that first named this conference; null when the entry carries no fully specified date
distributed.title: Distributed

transition.description: How the petition reached this conference: `first` (its first distribution); `relist` (the conference before sat on the petition and left it undecided, and this entry was docketed after that conference and within 14 days of it); `reschedule` (the conference before never sat on it: this entry was docketed before that conference day, or a call for response or a 'Rescheduled' entry took the petition off it first); `redistributed` (the conference before sat, and this entry came more than 14 days later, as after a hold or an invited brief); `after_decision` (docketed after the petition was decided, as for rehearing); `unknown` (the entry's date will not parse, or it is the conference day itself, which cannot say whether the conference had sat, or it names a conference no later than the one before)
transition.title: Transition

ConferenceStep.title: ConferenceStep

ScheduleEntry.description:
One pending, already-public docket's next dates at the Court.

A row exists for every docket on the public set that has at least one of
three dates in play: the conference an undecided petition is distributed
for, the day a granted case awaiting its merits decision is set for
argument, and the deadline for a response that is still owed. Each date is
published only while it falls on or after the schedule's `as_of`; once it
has passed and the docket has not moved, the row keeps the date as read and
says why it is no longer a scheduled date, so a past date is never shown as
upcoming.

argument.description: The day the docket's newest 'SET FOR ARGUMENT on …' entry names, on a granted case the Court has not yet decided. Null when the case is not set for argument, or has been argued on or after that day

conferences.description: Every conference the petition was distributed for, in docket order, each with how it got there (`relist`, `reschedule`, …). History, never a scheduled date: the upcoming one is `next_conference`. Null on a 1.1 row, on an application (the history is read for cert petitions only), and where the live channel has not read the history since it was first kept; an empty list on a docket never distributed
conferences.title: Conferences

distributed_for_conference.description: The corpus `distributed_for_conference`: the date named by the docket's newest 'DISTRIBUTED for Conference of …' entry, as the live channel last read it, whether or not it has passed. Null on an undecided docket never distributed, and on a granted case, whose conference is behind it
distributed_for_conference.title: Distributed For Conference

last_live_polled.description: When the live channel last read this docket — the per-case vintage of every date on the row, which `as_of` is not
last_live_polled.title: Last Live Polled

next_conference.description: The conference the docket is distributed for, when it falls on or after `as_of`; null when `stale_reason` is set, and when the row names no conference (`distributed_for_conference` null)
next_conference.title: Next Conference

relists.description: How many times the Court relisted the petition: the `conferences` steps marked `relist`. Exact, and at most the number of conferences less one. Null exactly when `conferences` is
relists.title: Relists

response_due.description: The newest stated deadline for a response to the petition or application, while the docket is undecided and the response is still owed. Null when no deadline is stated, or a response or waiver followed it

stale_reason.description: Why the row carries no `next_conference` although it names a conference: `conference_passed` (the conference is before `as_of` and the docket shows no newer distribution or a decision yet). Null while the date is still ahead, and on a row that names no conference
stale_reason.title: Stale Reason

ScheduleEntry.title: ScheduleEntry

ScheduledDay.description:
One date the Court has set on a docket, as the live channel last read it.

`upcoming` carries the date only while it falls on or after the schedule's
`as_of`; once it has passed, the row keeps the date as read in `set_for`
and says why it is no longer scheduled, so a past date is never shown as
upcoming.

set_for.description: The date the docket names, whether or not it has passed
set_for.title: Set For

stale_reason.description: Why the day carries no `upcoming` date: `passed` (`set_for` is before `as_of`, and the docket shows no newer setting yet). Null while the date is ahead
stale_reason.title: Stale Reason

upcoming.description: `set_for`, when it falls on or after `as_of`; null exactly when `stale_reason` is set
upcoming.title: Upcoming

ScheduledDay.title: ScheduledDay

description:
``data/schedule/schedule.json`` — the Court's next dates, public set only.

Written by the live poll from the corpus it already holds, after each cycle,
for the dockets the repository already discloses under ``data/cases``: it is
enumerated from that committed tree alone and never from a corpus scan, the
same compilation-extent boundary as the scope manifest. Display data for
the public site: it is not a prediction-ledger record (a schedule moves on
every relist), nothing predicts, evaluates or scores on it, and no cell is
provisioned with it. ``skipped`` is set, with no entries, when no corpus was
present.

as_of.description: The UTC day the schedule was built on, which decides whether a date has passed; null on a skipped build
as_of.title: As Of

court_next_conference.description: The Court's first conference on or after `as_of`, read from the committed term calendar (`data/schedule/term-calendar.json`) whether or not any public docket is distributed for it; null when no calendar is committed or it names no conference that far ahead
court_next_conference.title: Court Next Conference

entries.description: One entry per pending public docket with a conference, an argument day or a response deadline in play, in case_id order
entries.title: Entries

schema_version.description: The artifact's schema version. A reader keys on it: a `1.1` row adds `argument` and `response_due`, and may name no conference; a `1.2` row adds `conferences` and `relists`; `1.3` adds the court-wide `court_next_conference`
schema_version.title: Schema Version

skipped.description: True when no corpus was present; nothing was read
skipped.title: Skipped

title: Schedule
